newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: France accuses rioters of destabilising French Guiana.
newsitem.headline: France accuses rioters of destabilising French Guiana.

text.p: Riots raged overnight in the French Guiana capital Cayenne for a third time within a week, and authorities on Wednesday accused violent groups of trying to destabilise the South American territory.
Riot police fired teargas at stone-throwing crowds, and battled for several hours to push them back to the outskirts.
Officials said rioters hurled petrol bombs at the home of the state prosecutor and looted a weapons shop.
Prefect (government representative) Pierre Dartout said the violence was led by well-organised groups hitting pre-selected targets.
"These are planned actions intended to destabilise (French) Guiana," he told local radio.
There were no immediate reports of casualties.

The latest violence erupted when a court convicted seven people arrested during riots last week which left one dead, at least six injured and caused millions of dollars in damage to government buildings and shops.
At the announcement of the verdict, bands of youths began to overturn garbage cans, break store windows and attempted to charge the local courthouse.
Paris flew 200 paramilitary riot police reinforcements to the territory, on the northeast coast of South America, over the weekend after local police were overwhelmed by the rioting.

Airport officials told Reuters all incoming and outgoing flights at French Guiana's international airport near Cayenne were cancelled on Wednesday. Air France said it cancelled its two flights to Cayenne, from Paris and Guadeloupe.

Airline sources said they feared airport services in Cayenne would be disrupted by a general strike called by an inter-union group protesting government policy in French Guiana and the arrest of the seven convicted rioters.
High school students protesting against poor conditions in local schools sparked the riots when their strike degenerated into clashes between police and youths.
The French government has promised to hold wide-ranging talks next year on the situation in French Guiana.

Jean-Jacques de Peretti, minister of overseas territories, said he would visit Guiana shortly with Education Minister Francois Bayrou and organise a conference there next year, "because the future of the Guianese is a matter for the Guianese themselves."
De Peretti told the National Assembly that the problems of French Guiana stemmed largely from illegal immigration and a sharp increase in population to 140,000 from 80,000 over the past 13 years.

French Guiana is the only non-independent territory in South America. Its economy lags behind that of mainland France, and it has an unemployment rate approaching 25 percent of the labour force. Joblessness is particularly acute among the young.
